definition_en: a group of parents and children, a line of relatives, or a group in biology
core_image: 周末的餐桌上，几代人围坐在一起，笑声不断
scene: 周末，一家人围坐在餐桌旁吃饭。The whole family sat around the table for dinner.
sceneCN: 这里 family 是「家庭」（第 1 个义项）；句意：全家人围坐桌旁吃晚饭。

senses.title: Parents and children
senses.definition: a group made up of parents and their children
senses.definitionCN: 由父母及其子女组成的群体
senses.example: The family eats dinner together every night.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人每晚一起吃晚饭。
senses.why: The core sense is the household of parents and children.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是父母与子女组成的家庭。

senses.title: Line of relatives
senses.definition: all the people related to one another across generations
senses.definitionCN: 跨世代相互有亲缘关系的所有人
senses.example: The family has lived here for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个家族在这里住了几个世纪。
senses.why: The household extends into a line of ancestors and relatives.
senses.whyCN: 家庭扩展为祖先与亲属的血脉。

senses.title: Biological group
senses.definition: a group of related plants or animals above genus and below order
senses.definitionCN: 亲缘植物或动物的分类单元，位于属之上、目之下
senses.example: The rose belongs to the rose family.
senses.exampleCN: 玫瑰属于蔷薇科。
senses.why: Related species form a kind of family tree.
senses.whyCN: 相关物种形成一种家族树。

senses.title: Language group
senses.definition: a group of languages that developed from a common ancestor
senses.definitionCN: 由共同祖语发展而来的一组语言
senses.example: French and Spanish belong to the same language family.
senses.exampleCN: 法语和西班牙语属于同一语族。
senses.why: Languages also have parents and descendants.
senses.whyCN: 语言也有父母与后代。

intro.en: Family comes from Latin familia, a household, which included servants as well as relatives.
intro.cn: family 源自拉丁语 familia（家户），既包括亲属也包括仆役。

items.en: Famulus meant a servant or household member.
items.cn: famulus 意为仆役或家户成员。

items.en: Familia meant the whole household.
items.cn: familia 意为整个家户。

items.en: Famille narrowed to parents, children, and relatives.
items.cn: famille 缩小为父母、子女与亲属。

items.en: Family named a household and a line of descent.
items.cn: family 指家户与血统世系。

items.en: Science borrowed family for related species.
items.cn: 科学借 family 表示相关物种。

items.en: Family now covers households, relatives, and groups.
items.cn: 现代英语中 family 涵盖家庭、亲属与分类群。

note.en: Family is compared with similar spellings and with words for households and relatives.
note.cn: 把 family 与形近词以及表示家庭和亲属的词作比较。

entries.definition: all the people living in one house
people connected by blood or marriage
a large group of related families

normalIntro.en: Family begins with fam, like familiar, because family are the people we know best.
normalIntro.cn: family 以 fam 开头，像 familiar，因为家人是我们最熟悉的人。

normal.en: Family and familiar share fam, the people closest to us.
normal.cn: family 与 familiar 共享 fam，都是最亲近的人。

normal.en: The plural families changes y to ies.
normal.cn: 复数 families 要把 y 变成 ies。

normal.en: Family name is another way to say surname.
normal.cn: family name 是姓氏的另一种说法。

normal.en: A family tree shows how relatives connect.
normal.cn: 家谱树显示亲属如何相连。

normal.en: In biology, a family sits above genus and below order.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，科位于属之上、目之下。

abstract.en: Family is the first group that teaches us who we are.
abstract.cn: 家庭是第一个教我们认识自己的群体。

abstract.en: The word once meant a whole household, servants included.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指包括仆役在内的整个家户。

abstract.en: Every field has families, from roses to languages.
abstract.cn: 从玫瑰到语言，每个领域都有「科」或「语族」。

examples.en: Her family moved to the city last year.
examples.cn: 她家去年搬到了城里。

examples.en: The whole family gathers at the grandparents' house.
examples.cn: 全家人聚在祖父母家。

examples.en: The cat is a member of the cat family.
examples.cn: 猫是猫科动物的一员。

dict_mnemonic.text: family 与 familiar 都含 fam，家人是最熟悉的人；此外科学分类中的「科」和语言学的「语族」也用 family。

root: 源自拉丁语 familia（家户），更早与 famulus（仆役）相关，核心义「共同生活、相互关联的一群人」。

sensesIntro.en: Family means parents and children, a line of relatives, a biological family, or a language family.
sensesIntro.cn: family 意为父母子女组成的家庭、家族亲属、生物分类的科，或语族。

core.en: A group joined by household or descent.
core.cn: 由共同生活或血统连接的一群。

branches.en: The everyday household of parents and children.
branches.cn: 父母子女的日常家庭。

branches.en: The wider line of relatives across generations.
branches.cn: 跨世代的更广泛亲属血脉。

branches.en: Related species grouped in biology.
branches.cn: 生物学中归为一类的相关物种。

branches.en: Related languages grouped by common origin.
branches.cn: 按共同来源归类的相关语言。

branches.en: The household is the nearest part of the wider family.
branches.cn: 家庭是更大亲属范围中最近的一环。

intro.en: Family forms adjectives about home life and suitability.
intro.cn: family 构成表示家庭生活和适用性的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin familia and famulus lie behind the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 familia 与 famulus 是英语 family 的来源。

items.meaning: a group of parents and children

items.exampleCN: 他们买了一个家庭装披萨。
这家酒店适合家庭入住。

items.example: Family life is important to them.
items.exampleCN: 家庭生活对他们很重要。

definition_en: known and recognized by many people
core_image: 广场上人们围着一位作家签名，记者不停拍照
scene: 这座小城因桥而闻名。The small town is famous for its bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 famous 是「以……闻名的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这座小城因它的桥而闻名。

senses.title: Known by many
senses.definition: known and recognized by a very large number of people
senses.definitionCN: 被非常多的人知道和认可的
senses.example: She is a famous singer.
senses.exampleCN: 她是一位著名歌手。
senses.why: The core sense is wide public recognition.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是广泛的公众认知。

senses.title: Well known for
senses.definition: recognized because of a particular quality or feature
senses.definitionCN: 因某一特定品质或特征而被人所知
senses.example: The town is famous for its bread.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小镇以面包闻名。
senses.why: Recognition attaches to a specific trait.
senses.whyCN: 名声附着在某个具体特征上。

senses.title: Widely known fact
senses.definition: known by most people in a place or group
senses.definitionCN: 被某地或某群体中大多数人知道
senses.example: It is a famous story in the village.
senses.exampleCN: 这是村里广为人知的故事。
senses.why: Fame can belong to stories as well as people.
senses.whyCN: 名声不仅属于人，也属于故事。

intro.en: Famous comes from Latin fama, report or fame, through Old French fameus.
intro.cn: famous 经古法语 fameus 源自拉丁语 fama（传闻、名声）。

items.en: Fama meant report, rumour, or fame.
items.cn: fama 意为传闻、流言或名声。

items.en: Famosus meant much talked about.
items.cn: famosus 意为被广泛谈论的。

items.en: Fameus meant renowned.
items.cn: fameus 意为有名的。

items.en: Famous named people and places of note.
items.cn: famous 指有名的人和地方。

items.en: Famous is often paired with for to name the reason.
items.cn: 现代英语中 famous 常与 for 搭配说明原因。

note.en: Famous is compared with similar spellings and with words for being well known.
note.cn: 把 famous 与形近词以及表示知名的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Famous comes from fame plus ous, full of fame.
normalIntro.cn: famous 由 fame 加 ous 构成，意为充满名声的。

normal.en: Fame plus ous means full of fame.
normal.cn: fame 加 ous 意为充满名声的。

normal.en: Famous for names the reason, as in famous for its bread.
normal.cn: famous for 说明原因，如 famous for its bread。

normal.en: World-famous adds world to show the scale.
normal.cn: world-famous 加上 world 表示范围。

normal.en: Infamous is the dark twin, famous for something bad.
normal.cn: infamous 是阴暗的孪生词，指因坏事出名。

normal.en: Famously can mean in a way everyone knows.
normal.cn: famously 可以表示众所周知地。

abstract.en: Fame is a story many people tell about you.
abstract.cn: 名声是许多人讲述的关于你的故事。

abstract.en: To be famous is to be seen, not necessarily known.
abstract.cn: 出名是被看见，而不一定被了解。

abstract.en: A famous place belongs partly to everyone who visits.
abstract.cn: 著名的地方部分属于每个来访者。

examples.en: The city is famous for its old walls.
examples.cn: 这座城市因古城墙而闻名。

examples.en: He became famous almost overnight.
examples.cn: 他几乎一夜成名。

examples.en: Many famous artists studied in this school.
examples.cn: 许多著名艺术家曾在这所学校学习。

dict_mnemonic.text: famous 是 fame（名声）加 -ous（充满……的），即「充满名声的、被很多人知道的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 fama（传闻、名声），famous 即「被广泛谈论、广为人知的」。

sensesIntro.en: Famous means known by many people, known for a particular quality, or widely known in a group.
sensesIntro.cn: famous 意为被许多人知道、因某特点而闻名，或在某群体中广为人知。

core.en: Widely known and talked about.
core.cn: 被广泛知道和谈论。

branches.en: The core state of being widely recognized.
branches.cn: 被广泛认可的核心状态。

branches.en: Recognition attached to a specific quality.
branches.cn: 附着于特定品质的名声。

branches.en: Stories and facts known by a whole group.
branches.cn: 整个群体都知道的故事与事实。

branches.en: Wide recognition usually has a reason behind it.
branches.cn: 广泛的知名度通常有其原因。

branches.en: People and stories can both be famous.
branches.cn: 人和故事都可以是著名的。

intro.en: Famous has a family built on fame and its absence.
intro.cn: famous 有围绕名声及其反面的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fama, report, is the root of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fama（传闻）是该词族的词根。

items.exampleCN: 她众所周知地拒绝了奖项。

items.example: The place is infamous for its crimes.
items.exampleCN: 这个地方因犯罪而臭名昭著。
这是一座世界闻名的博物馆。

items.example: The region is famous for tea.

definition_en: a device that moves air, a supporter of someone, or a folding object for cooling
core_image: 夏夜客厅里，风扇叶片呼呼转动，送来阵阵凉风
scene: 天太热了，他把风扇开到最大。He turned the fan up to full speed.
sceneCN: 这里 fan 是「风扇」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他把风扇调到最高档。

senses.title: Air-moving device
senses.definition: a machine with rotating blades that moves air to cool a room
senses.definitionCN: 带旋转叶片、用来送风降温的机器
senses.example: The fan makes the room bearable in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天风扇让房间变得可以忍受。
senses.why: The core mechanical sense is a device that creates a breeze.
senses.whyCN: 核心机械义是制造凉风的装置。

senses.title: Folding cooler
senses.definition: a hand-held object that is waved to create cool air
senses.definitionCN: 手持挥动以产生凉风的物件
senses.example: She cooled herself with a paper fan.
senses.exampleCN: 她用纸扇给自己扇风。
senses.why: The old hand tool shares the air-moving shape and purpose.
senses.whyCN: 古老的手持工具共享送风的形状与用途。

senses.title: Enthusiastic supporter
senses.definition: a person who strongly admires a team, star, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 强烈崇拜某队、明星或活动的人
senses.example: He is a lifelong fan of the club.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这家俱乐部的终身粉丝。
senses.why: A fan is as constant and energetic as a cooling fan.
senses.whyCN: 粉丝像风扇一样持续而热烈。

senses.title: Create a breeze
senses.definition: to wave something to create air, or to make a feeling stronger
senses.definitionCN: 挥动某物产生气流，或使某种情绪更强烈
senses.example: She fanned the fire with a newspaper.
senses.exampleCN: 她用报纸扇火。
senses.why: The device action extends to stirring up feelings.
senses.whyCN: 装置的动作扩展到煽动情绪。

intro.en: Fan comes from Latin vannus, a winnowing basket, through Old English fann.
intro.cn: fan 经古英语 fann 源自拉丁语 vannus（扬谷篮）。

items.en: Vannus meant a basket for winnowing grain.
items.cn: vannus 意为扬谷用的篮子。

items.en: Vannare meant to winnow by tossing grain in the air.
items.cn: vannare 意为把谷物抛向空中扬场。

items.en: Fann named a basket or fan for winnowing.
items.cn: fann 指扬场用的篮子或扇具。

items.en: Fan extended to hand-held cooling objects.
items.cn: fan 扩展到手持的取凉物件。

items.en: The word gained the sense of an enthusiastic supporter.
items.cn: 该词获得狂热爱好者的含义。

items.en: Fan covers machines, hand tools, and admirers.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fan 涵盖机器、手工具与崇拜者。

note.en: Fan is compared with similar spellings and with words for supporters and air movers.
note.cn: 把 fan 与形近词以及表示支持者和送风装置的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who backs a team or cause
a person who likes someone greatly

normalIntro.en: Fan began as a basket waved to winnow grain.
normalIntro.cn: fan 最初指扬谷时挥动的篮子。

normal.en: A fan moves air, and a fan of a star moves with excitement.
normal.cn: 风扇送风，明星的粉丝也热情涌动。

normal.en: Fan the flames is a literal and figurative phrase.
normal.cn: fan the flames 既可指扇火，也可指煽动情绪。

normal.en: The double n appears in fanned and fanning.
normal.cn: fanned 和 fanning 中有双写 n。

normal.en: A ceiling fan hangs above; an electric fan stands on the floor.
normal.cn: 吊扇挂在上面，电扇立在地上。

normal.en: A football fan cheers for the team.
normal.cn: 足球迷为球队欢呼。

abstract.en: A fan turns still air into a breeze.
abstract.cn: 风扇把静止的空气变成微风。

abstract.en: Enthusiasm spreads like air from a fan.
abstract.cn: 热情像风扇送出的风一样传播。

abstract.en: The same word cools a room and warms a crowd.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能让房间变凉，也能让一群人热血沸腾。

examples.en: Please turn on the fan; it is hot in here.
examples.cn: 请打开风扇，这里很热。

examples.en: She used a fan to cool her face.
examples.cn: 她用扇子给脸扇风。

examples.en: Thousands of fans waited outside the theatre.
examples.cn: 数千名粉丝在剧院外等候。

dict_mnemonic.text: fan 原指扬谷的扇篮，后来指风扇、扇子；热情持续的人像风扇一样围着偶像转，就是粉丝。

root: 源自拉丁语 vannus（扬谷篮），经古英语 fann 入英语，核心义「挥动送风的器具」，引申为狂热爱好者。

sensesIntro.en: Fan means an air-moving machine, a hand-held cooler, an enthusiastic supporter, or to create a breeze.
sensesIntro.cn: fan 意为风扇、扇子、狂热爱好者，或扇风、煽动。

core.en: Something waved or spinning to move air.
core.cn: 挥动或旋转以送风的东西。

branches.en: The modern machine that cools a room.
branches.cn: 给房间降温的现代机器。

branches.en: The old hand tool for cooling.
branches.cn: 古老的取凉手工具。

branches.en: A person who admires someone or something.
branches.cn: 崇拜某人或某物的人。

branches.en: The act of waving to create air or stir feelings.
branches.cn: 挥动产生气流或激起情绪的动作。

branches.en: The machine and the hand both move air.
branches.cn: 机器与手都在送风。

intro.en: Fan forms words for groups, extremists, and shapes.
intro.cn: fan 构成表示群体、狂热者和形状的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vannus, a winnowing basket, is the distant source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vannus（扬谷篮）是远源。

items.example: She fanned the soup to cool it.
Fanning the fire made it grow.

items.meaning: a fan fixed to a ceiling

definition_en: elaborate and decorative, imagined rather than real, or to want something
core_image: 橱窗里一条缀满亮片和蕾丝的连衣裙，精致得不太日常
scene: 她穿了一条别致的连衣裙去参加晚会。She wore a fancy dress to the party.
sceneCN: 这里 fancy 是「别致的；花哨的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她穿了一条别致的连衣裙去参加晚会。

senses.title: Elaborate and decorative
senses.definition: unusually elaborate, decorated, or complicated
senses.definitionCN: 不同寻常地精致、装饰繁复或复杂的
senses.example: The cake had fancy decorations.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋糕上有精致的装饰。
senses.why: The core sense is more decoration than necessary.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是超出必要的装饰。

senses.title: Expensive and upscale
senses.definition: of high quality and cost, often too expensive for everyday use
senses.definitionCN: 质量与价格都高，常超出日常所需
senses.example: They ate at a fancy hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一家高档酒店用餐。
senses.why: Elaboration becomes a mark of luxury.
senses.whyCN: 精致成为奢华的标志。

senses.title: Imagination
senses.definition: the power of imagining things, or something imagined
senses.definitionCN: 想象事物的能力，或想象出的东西
senses.example: The story is a product of fancy.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事是想象的产物。
senses.why: Decoration and imagination both go beyond plain fact.
senses.whyCN: 装饰与想象都超出平淡的事实。

senses.title: Want or like
senses.definition: to want something or feel like doing it, used in informal British English
senses.definitionCN: 想要某物或想做某事，用于非正式英式英语
senses.example: Do you fancy a cup of tea?
senses.exampleCN: 你想喝杯茶吗？
senses.why: A passing wish is a fancy in motion.
senses.whyCN: 一时的愿望就是行动中的幻想。

intro.en: Fancy is a shortened form of fantasy, from Greek phantasia, imagination.
intro.cn: fancy 是 fantasy 的缩略形式，源自希腊语 phantasia（想象）。

items.en: Phantasia meant appearance or imagination.
items.cn: phantasia 意为显现或想象。

items.en: Phantasia meant imagination or a phantom.
items.cn: phantasia 意为想象或幻影。

items.en: Fantaisie meant imagination or a whim.
items.cn: fantaisie 意为想象或一时兴致。

items.en: Fantasie and fantsy named imagination.
items.cn: fantasie 与 fantsy 指想象力。

items.en: Fancy shortened the word and added the sense of taste.
items.cn: fancy 缩短了词形，并增加品味之义。

items.en: Fancy covers decoration, luxury, imagination, and desire.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fancy 涵盖装饰、奢华、想象与愿望。

note.en: Fancy is compared with similar spellings and with words for decoration and imagination.
note.cn: 把 fancy 与形近词以及表示装饰和想象的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fancy is fantasy shortened, so it keeps the shine of imagination.
normalIntro.cn: fancy 是 fantasy 的缩略，仍保留想象的光泽。

normal.en: Fancy is fantasy minus tasy, a quicker way to say imagination.
normal.cn: fancy 是 fantasy 去掉 tasy，是想象的快捷说法。

normal.en: Fancy dress can mean a costume or an elaborate dress.
normal.cn: fancy dress 既可指化装服，也可指别致的连衣裙。

normal.en: A fancy restaurant is expensive and decorated.
normal.cn: fancy restaurant 是高档且装饰讲究的餐厅。

normal.en: Do you fancy tea means do you want tea.
normal.cn: Do you fancy tea 意为你想喝茶吗。

normal.en: Fanciful means full of imagination.
normal.cn: fanciful 意为充满想象的。

abstract.en: Fancy is the mind adding decoration to plain reality.
abstract.cn: fancy 是心灵给平淡现实添加装饰。

abstract.en: A fancy is a wish that has not yet asked permission.
abstract.cn: 幻想是尚未征求许可的愿望。

abstract.en: The word links what looks rich with what is imagined.
abstract.cn: 这个词把看起来华丽的东西与想象之物连接起来。

examples.en: She fancied a walk along the river.
examples.cn: 她想沿河散散步。

examples.en: The shop sells fancy cakes and chocolates.
examples.cn: 这家店卖精致的蛋糕和巧克力。

examples.en: His story was pure fancy.
examples.cn: 他的故事纯属想象。

dict_mnemonic.text: fancy 是 fantasy 的缩写，本义「想象」；想象出来的东西往往花哨精致，于是又有「别致、高档」和「想要」的意思。

root: 由 fantasy 缩略而来，源自希腊语 phantasia（想象），核心义「脱离平淡现实的想象与装饰」。

sensesIntro.en: Fancy means elaborate or upscale, imagination, or to want something in informal British English.
sensesIntro.cn: fancy 意为精致花哨或高档、想象，或在非正式英式英语中表示想要。

core.en: Imagination that adds colour beyond plain fact.
core.cn: 在平淡事实之外增添色彩的想象。

branches.en: Decoration makes an object elaborate.
branches.cn: 装饰使物品变得精致。

branches.en: Elaboration becomes a sign of luxury.
branches.cn: 精致成为奢华的标志。

branches.en: The original sense of imagination remains.
branches.cn: 想象的本义仍然保留。

branches.en: A sudden wish is imagination turned toward action.
branches.cn: 一时的愿望是转向行动的想象。

branches.en: Both decoration and imagination go beyond the plain.
branches.cn: 装饰与想象都超越平淡。

intro.en: Fancy has a family of imagination and decoration.
intro.cn: fancy 有围绕想象与装饰的词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek phantasia and Latin phantasia are the distant roots.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 phantasia 与拉丁语 phantasia 是远源。

items.example: It is the fanciest hotel in town.
items.exampleCN: 这是城里最高档的酒店。
她想要一个安静的夜晚。

items.example: The fanciness of the dress surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 这条裙子的花哨让我们吃惊。

definition_en: extremely good, or strange and imagined rather than real
core_image: 舞台灯光亮起，观众全体起立，为一场精彩演出欢呼
scene: 演出结束后，观众高喊太棒了。The crowd shouted that the show was fantastic.
sceneCN: 这里 fantastic 是「极好的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：观众高喊这场演出太棒了。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: extremely good or enjoyable, used in informal praise
senses.definitionCN: 极好或令人愉快的，用于非正式赞扬
senses.example: We had a fantastic time at the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在海滩度过了极好的时光。
senses.why: The core modern sense is strong approval.
senses.whyCN: 核心现代义是强烈的赞许。

senses.title: Strange and imagined
senses.definition: strange, unlikely, or produced by imagination rather than reality
senses.definitionCN: 奇怪、不太可能，或由想象而非现实产生
senses.example: The story features fantastic creatures.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里有奇异的生物。
senses.why: The older sense is something beyond the ordinary world.
senses.whyCN: 较古老的义项是超出寻常世界的事物。

senses.title: Enormously large
senses.definition: very large in amount or degree, often surprisingly so
senses.definitionCN: 数量或程度上非常大，常令人惊讶
senses.example: The project was a fantastic amount of work.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目的工作量大得惊人。
senses.why: What exceeds imagination also exceeds ordinary size.
senses.whyCN: 超出想象的东西也超出寻常规模。

intro.en: Fantastic comes from Greek phantastikos, able to imagine, through Latin.
intro.cn: fantastic 经拉丁语源自希腊语 phantastikos（能想象的）。

items.en: Phantastikos meant able to form images in the mind.
items.cn: phantastikos 意为能在心中形成形象的。

items.en: Phantasticus meant imaginary or unreal.
items.cn: phantasticus 意为想象中的、不真实的。

items.en: Fantastic meant existing only in imagination.
items.cn: fantastic 意为只存在于想象中的。

items.en: The word described strange and exaggerated things.
items.cn: 该词形容奇异夸张的事物。

items.en: Fantastic also became a strong word of praise.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fantastic 也成为强烈的赞美词。

note.en: Fantastic is compared with similar spellings and with words for praise and strangeness.
note.cn: 把 fantastic 与形近词以及表示赞美和奇异的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fantastic comes from fantasy, so it means both imagined wonders and real delight.
normalIntro.cn: fantastic 源自 fantasy，既指想象中的奇妙，也指现实的喜悦。

normal.en: Fantastic and fantasy share the fan sound.
normal.cn: fantastic 与 fantasy 共享 fan 的音。

normal.en: A fantastic meal is almost too good to be real.
normal.cn: 一顿极好的饭几乎好得不真实。

normal.en: Fantastic creatures belong to fantasy stories.
normal.cn: 奇异生物属于奇幻故事。

normal.en: Fantastically means in an amazing way.
normal.cn: fantastically 意为以惊人的方式。

normal.en: In speech, fantastic often simply means very good.
normal.cn: 在口语中 fantastic 常常只表示很好。

abstract.en: Fantastic things stretch what we think is possible.
abstract.cn: 奇妙之物拓展我们对可能性的认知。

abstract.en: Praise and wonder share one word.
abstract.cn: 赞美与惊奇共用一个词。

abstract.en: The word began in the mind and now describes the world.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于心灵，如今用来描述世界。

examples.en: The view from the top was fantastic.
examples.cn: 山顶的景色美极了。

examples.en: She came up with a fantastic plan.
examples.cn: 她想出了一个绝妙计划。

examples.en: The novel is full of fantastic animals.
examples.cn: 这部小说满是奇异的动物。

dict_mnemonic.text: fantastic 与 fantasy 同源，本义「只存在于想象中的」；想象中最好的东西，就是口语里的「棒极了」。

root: 源自希腊语 phantastikos（能想象的），经拉丁语 phantasticus 入英语，核心义「超出寻常、仿佛出自想象」。

sensesIntro.en: Fantastic means extremely good, strange and imagined, or surprisingly large.
sensesIntro.cn: fantastic 意为极好的、奇异想象的，或数量惊人的。

core.en: Something beyond the ordinary, whether wonderful or strange.
core.cn: 超出寻常的事物，无论美妙还是奇异。

branches.en: The modern sense of strong approval.
branches.cn: 强烈赞许的现代义。

branches.en: The older sense of strange imagination.
branches.cn: 奇异想象的古老义。

branches.en: Something so large it seems unreal.
branches.cn: 大到显得不真实的程度。

branches.en: Praise and surprise both exceed the ordinary.
branches.cn: 赞美与惊奇都超出寻常。

branches.en: Imagined things are often exaggerated in size.
branches.cn: 想象之物常在大小上被夸张。

intro.en: Fantastic belongs to the fantasy family of imagination.
intro.cn: fantastic 属于 fantasy 的想象词族。

latinIntro.en: Greek phantasia and Latin phantasticus are the roots.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 phantasia 与拉丁语 phantasticus 是词根。

items.example: The fantasist created a new world.
items.exampleCN: 这位奇幻作家创造了一个新世界。

items.example: The hotel has a fantastic view.

definition_en: at a long distance, or by a great amount
core_image: 一条公路笔直延伸到地平线，远处的山只剩淡淡轮廓
scene: 车站离家很远，他每天骑车去。The station is far from his home.
sceneCN: 这里 far 是「远的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：车站离他家很远。

senses.title: At a great distance
senses.definition: at or to a long distance from a place or person
senses.definitionCN: 离某地或某人很远或在很远之处
senses.example: They walked far into the forest.
senses.exampleCN: 他们走进森林深处。
senses.why: The core sense is physical distance.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是空间距离。

senses.title: By a great amount
senses.definition: used before a comparative to show a large difference
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较级前表示很大差别
senses.example: This method is far better.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法好得多。
senses.why: Distance in space becomes distance in degree.
senses.whyCN: 空间距离引申为程度差距。

senses.title: Distant in space
senses.definition: located a long way away
senses.definitionCN: 位于很远之处的
senses.example: He lives in a far country.
senses.exampleCN: 他住在一个遥远的国家。
senses.why: The adverb sense appears as an adjective before a noun.
senses.whyCN: 副词义以形容词形式出现在名词前。

senses.title: Distant in time
senses.definition: a long time away in the past or future
senses.definitionCN: 在过去或未来很久远的时间
senses.example: The day is not far off.
senses.exampleCN: 那一天不远了。
senses.why: Distance in space stretches to distance in time.
senses.whyCN: 空间距离延伸到时间距离。

intro.en: Far is a native English word from Old English feor, with Germanic roots.
intro.cn: far 是英语本族词，源自古英语 feor，属日耳曼语源。

items.en: Ferro meant distant.
items.cn: ferro 意为遥远的。

items.en: Feor meant far or distant.
items.cn: feor 意为远的、遥远的。

items.en: Fer and far both appeared in writing.
items.cn: fer 与 far 都出现在书面语中。

items.en: Far became the standard spelling.
items.cn: far 成为标准拼写。

items.en: Far is used for distance and for degree.
items.cn: 现代英语中 far 既表距离也表程度。

note.en: Far is compared with similar spellings and with words for distance.
note.cn: 把 far 与形近词以及表示距离的词作比较。

entries.definition: the oily substance in the body

normalIntro.en: Far is short, just like the distance it often describes is long.
normalIntro.cn: far 很短，却常用来描述很长的距离。

normal.en: Far away means at a great distance.
normal.cn: far away 意为在很远的地方。

normal.en: So far means until now.
normal.cn: so far 意为到目前为止。

normal.en: Far better means much better.
normal.cn: far better 意为好得多。

normal.en: Farther is for distance, further for degree.
normal.cn: farther 多指距离，further 多指程度。

normal.en: As far as I know introduces a limit on knowledge.
normal.cn: as far as I know 引出认知的界限。

abstract.en: Far measures the space between here and there.
abstract.cn: far 衡量此处与彼处之间的空间。

abstract.en: The same word measures distance and difference.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既衡量距离也衡量差别。

abstract.en: What is far in space can feel near in memory.
abstract.cn: 空间上遥远的东西在记忆中可能很近。

examples.en: The airport is too far to walk.
examples.cn: 机场太远，走不到。

examples.en: This solution is far simpler.
examples.cn: 这个解决办法简单得多。

examples.en: We have not gone far enough.
examples.cn: 我们走得还不够远。

dict_mnemonic.text: far 是本族词，无前缀后缀；记住三组常用短语：far away、so far、far from。

root: 源自古英语 feor（远的），属日耳曼语源，核心义「空间或程度上的距离大」。

sensesIntro.en: Far means at a great distance, by a great amount, or distant in space or time.
sensesIntro.cn: far 意为在远处、程度上……得多，或空间与时间上遥远。

core.en: A large distance between two points.
core.cn: 两点之间的巨大距离。

branches.en: The core adverbial sense of distance.
branches.cn: 表示距离的核心副词义。

branches.en: A large gap in degree or quality.
branches.cn: 程度或质量上的巨大差距。

branches.en: A place located a long way away.
branches.cn: 位于很远之处的地方。

branches.en: A time long before or after now.
branches.cn: 现在之前或之后的久远时间。

branches.en: Space and degree both use the image of distance.
branches.cn: 空间与程度都使用距离意象。

intro.en: Far has comparative and superlative forms with th.
intro.cn: far 有带 th 的比较级和最高级形式。

latinIntro.en: Far is Germanic, so no Latin root is listed.
latinIntro.cn: far 属日耳曼语，因此不列拉丁词根。

items.example: This is the furthest we can go.
items.exampleCN: 这是我们能走的最远一步。

items.example: The work is far from finished.

definition_en: an area of land used for growing crops or keeping animals, or to work such land
core_image: 清晨的农场，拖拉机驶过整齐的田垄，牛羊在远处吃草
scene: 天刚亮，他就开着拖拉机去农场干活。At dawn he drove his tractor to the farm to work.
sceneCN: 这里 farm 是「农场」（第 1 个义项）；句意：天刚亮，他就开着拖拉机去农场干活。

senses.title: Land for crops and animals
senses.definition: an area of land and buildings used for growing crops or keeping animals
senses.definitionCN: 用于种植作物或饲养牲畜的一片土地及建筑
senses.example: They keep cows and sheep on the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在农场里养奶牛和绵羊。
senses.why: The basic modern sense is a working piece of agricultural land.
senses.whyCN: 核心现代义就是一块用于农业生产的土地。

senses.title: A specialized production site
senses.definition: a place where a particular animal or crop is produced on a large scale
senses.definitionCN: 大规模生产某种动物或作物的场地
senses.example: The fish farm supplies the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 这家渔场供应整个地区。
senses.why: Specialized production narrows the land sense to one product.
senses.whyCN: 专业化生产把土地义缩小到单一产品。

senses.title: To work the land
senses.definition: to grow crops or keep animals as a business
senses.definitionCN: 以种植作物或饲养牲畜为业
senses.example: Her family has farmed this valley for generations.
senses.exampleCN: 她的家族在这个山谷里耕种了好几代。
senses.why: The verb turns the place into a continuing activity.
senses.whyCN: 动词义把场所变成持续进行的活动。

intro.en: Farm comes from Old English feorm, meaning food, supplies, or a rent paid in goods.
intro.cn: farm 源自古英语 feorm，意为食物、供给或用实物支付的地租。

items.en: Feorm meant food, supplies, or a rent paid in goods.
items.cn: feorm 意为食物、供给或用实物支付的地租。

items.en: Ferme came to mean land held for a fixed rent.
items.cn: ferme 开始表示按固定地租持有的土地。

items.en: The meaning shifted to land used for agriculture.
items.cn: 词义转向用于农业的土地。

items.en: Farm covered both the land and the business of working it.
items.cn: farm 同时指土地和经营土地的事业。

items.en: Farm is now the everyday word for agricultural land.
items.cn: 现代英语中 farm 是表示农业土地的日常用词。

note.en: Farm is compared with similar short words and with words for large agricultural places.
note.cn: 把 farm 与形近的短词以及表示大型农业场地的词作比较。

entries.definition: a shape, or a printed paper
the state of being well known
a large farm for cattle or horses
a large estate growing one crop

normalIntro.en: Farm is the place, farmer is the person, and farming is the work.
normalIntro.cn: farm 是场所，farmer 是人，farming 是工作。

normal.en: Farm hides the short word far plus an m.
normal.cn: farm 可以看成 far 后面加一个 m。

normal.en: A farmer works on a farm.
normal.cn: farmer 在 farm 上干活。

normal.en: A dairy farm produces milk.
normal.cn: 奶牛场生产牛奶。

normal.en: Farmland is the land of a farm.
normal.cn: farmland 就是农场的土地。

normal.en: The f at the start can stand for food.
normal.cn: 开头的 f 可以联想为 food（食物）。

abstract.en: The core of farm is not crops but support: land that feeds people.
abstract.cn: farm 的核心不是作物，而是供养：土地供养人。

abstract.en: From rent to cultivation, farm always concerns the use of land.
abstract.cn: 从地租到耕种，farm 始终围绕土地的使用权。

abstract.en: A farm is both a physical place and an economic unit.
abstract.cn: 农场既是地理空间，也是经济单位。

examples.en: The farm grows wheat and corn.
examples.cn: 这个农场种小麦和玉米。

examples.en: They run a small dairy farm.
examples.cn: 他们经营一个小型奶牛场。

examples.en: My grandfather farmed this land for forty years.
examples.cn: 我祖父在这片土地上耕种了四十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: farm 源自古英语 feorm（食物、地租），从「以食物交租的土地」演变为「农场」；加上表人的后缀就是 farmer。

root: 源自古英语 feorm（食物、供给、地租），核心义「供养人的土地与出产」。

sensesIntro.en: Farm means land for crops and animals, a specialized production site, or the work of cultivating land.
sensesIntro.cn: farm 意为种植养殖的土地、专业化生产场地，或耕种土地的行为。

core.en: A piece of land that feeds people.
core.cn: 一块供养人们的土地。

branches.en: Land that grows crops and keeps animals.
branches.cn: 种植作物、饲养牲畜的土地。

branches.en: A site devoted to one product, such as fish.
branches.cn: 专门生产一种产品的场地，如渔场。

branches.en: The activity of working such land.
branches.cn: 经营这类土地的活动。

branches.en: Both senses name a place of agricultural production.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指农业生产场所。

branches.en: The place and the work share the same word.
branches.cn: 场所与劳作共用同一个词。

intro.en: Farm builds a large English family for land, people, and buildings.
intro.cn: farm 构成一个包含土地、人物与建筑的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Old English feorm is the source; farm has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 feorm 是词源，farm 没有拉丁词根。

items.meaning: land for crops, or to work land

items.exampleCN: 这些田地采用有机方式耕种。

items.meaning: a person who runs a farm
the main house on a farm
items.exampleCN: 他们修复了一座老农舍。

definition_en: a person who owns or manages a farm, or who raises a particular animal or crop
core_image: 戴着草帽的农夫站在田埂上，身后是刚收割的麦田
scene: 农夫把一捆捆干草装上卡车。The farmer loaded bundles of hay onto the truck.
sceneCN: 这里 farmer 是「农夫；农场主」（第 1 个义项）；句意：农夫把一捆捆干草装上卡车。

senses.title: A person who runs a farm
senses.definition: a person who owns or manages a farm
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或经营农场的人
senses.example: The farmer rises before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫在日出前就起床。
senses.why: The core sense is the person in charge of farm land.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是负责经营农田的人。

senses.title: A specialist producer
senses.definition: a person who keeps a particular animal or grows a particular crop
senses.definitionCN: 饲养某种动物或种植某种作物的人
senses.example: She is a sheep farmer in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 她是山区的养羊户。
senses.why: The same role narrows to one kind of production.
senses.whyCN: 同一角色缩小到某一种生产活动。

intro.en: Farmer is farm plus the person suffix er, first meaning a tenant who paid rent for land.
intro.cn: farmer 由 farm 加表人的后缀 er 构成，最初指为土地交租的佃户。

items.en: Feorm, food or rent, named the land a tenant held.
items.cn: feorm（食物或地租）指佃户持有的土地。

items.en: A fermer was a tenant who paid rent for land.
items.cn: fermer 指为土地支付地租的佃户。

items.en: Farmer came to mean a person who worked agricultural land.
items.cn: farmer 开始指耕作农田的人。

items.en: The word spread to colonial and overseas farming.
items.cn: 该词随殖民与海外农业传播开来。

items.en: Farmer now means anyone who owns or runs a farm.
items.cn: 现代英语中 farmer 指任何拥有或经营农场的人。

note.en: Farmer is compared with similar-looking words and with other names for rural producers.
note.cn: 把 farmer 与形近词以及其他表示农村生产者的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who owns a large cattle farm
a person or tool that prepares land

normalIntro.en: Farmer is simply farm plus er, the suffix for a person who does something.
normalIntro.cn: farmer 就是 farm 加上表示做事之人的后缀 er。

normal.en: Farm is the land and farmer is the person.
normal.cn: farm 是土地，farmer 是人。

normal.en: A dairy farmer keeps cows for milk.
normal.cn: 奶牛场主养牛取奶。

normal.en: A farmer's market sells food from farms.
normal.cn: 农夫市场出售来自农场的食物。

normal.en: Farmer and farmhand both work with land.
normal.cn: farmer 与 farmhand 都与土地打交道。

normal.en: The er ending often marks a job.
normal.cn: er 结尾常表示一种职业。

abstract.en: The suffix er turns a place into a person: farm becomes farmer.
abstract.cn: 后缀 er 把场所变成人：farm 变成 farmer。

abstract.en: A farmer's link to land is management, not only labour.
abstract.cn: 农夫与土地的关系是经营，而不只是劳作。

abstract.en: Job names often compress a place into an identity.
abstract.cn: 职业名称常常把一个地方压缩成一种身份。

examples.en: The farmer keeps bees and sheep.
examples.cn: 这位农夫养蜂又养羊。

examples.en: Local farmers sell vegetables at the market.
examples.cn: 当地农夫在市场上卖蔬菜。

examples.en: A rice farmer works in water for hours.
examples.cn: 稻农在水里劳作数小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: farm 是「农场」，er 表示「做某事的人」，farmer 就是经营或耕作农场的人。

root: 由 farm（农场）加表人后缀 er 构成，farm 源自古英语 feorm（食物、地租）。

sensesIntro.en: Farmer means a person who owns or manages a farm, or one who raises a particular product.
sensesIntro.cn: farmer 意为拥有或经营农场的人，或专门养殖种植某种产品的人。

core.en: A person who works and manages agricultural land.
core.cn: 在土地上劳作并经营农业生产的人。

branches.en: The person in charge of the land.
branches.cn: 负责经营土地的人。

branches.en: The person who raises one product.
branches.cn: 专门养殖或种植一种产品的人。

branches.en: Both senses name a rural producer.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指农村生产者。

branches.en: Ownership and specialization can describe the same person.
branches.cn: 经营与专长可以描述同一个人。

branches.en: The role ranges from general manager to specialist.
branches.cn: 这一角色从综合经营者延伸到专业生产者。

intro.en: Farmer joins the farm family of land, work, and buildings.
intro.cn: farmer 加入由土地、劳作与建筑构成的 farm 词族。

latinIntro.en: The word is English throughout; feorm is its Old English source.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词完全是英语构词，feorm 是其古英语来源。

items.meaning: a person who runs a farm
land for crops, or to work land
a worker hired on a farm
items.exampleCN: 一名农场工人开着拖拉机。

items.meaning: a market selling farm food directly
items.example: The farmer's market opens on Saturday.

definition_en: to interest or attract someone very strongly, or to bewitch by magic in older use
core_image: 孩子趴在玻璃前，目不转睛地看一条盘绕的蛇
scene: 恐龙化石让全班同学着迷。Dinosaur fossils fascinate the whole class.
sceneCN: 这里 fascinate 是「使着迷」（第 1 个义项）；句意：恐龙化石让全班同学着迷。

senses.title: To attract strongly
senses.definition: to interest or attract someone very strongly
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地引起某人的兴趣或吸引某人
senses.example: The old photographs fascinate her.
senses.exampleCN: 那些老照片让她着迷。
senses.why: The main modern sense is intense, lasting interest.
senses.whyCN: 主要现代义是强烈而持久的兴趣。

senses.title: To hold the gaze
senses.definition: to hold someone's attention so that they cannot look away
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢抓住某人的注意力，使其无法移开视线
senses.example: The dancer's movement fascinated the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者的动作让观众看得目不转睛。
senses.why: The sense stresses attention fixed on one sight.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项强调注意力被固定在一个画面上。

senses.title: To bewitch
senses.definition: to put someone under a magic spell, in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 在较古老或文学用法中，用魔法迷住某人
senses.example: In the tale, a spirit fascinates the traveler.
senses.exampleCN: 故事里，一个精灵用魔法迷住了旅人。
senses.why: The original sense was literal magic.
senses.whyCN: 最初的义项就是字面意义上的魔法。

intro.en: Fascinate comes from Latin fascinare, to bewitch, and first meant to enchant by magic.
intro.cn: fascinate 源自拉丁语 fascinare（施魔法），最初意为用魔法迷住。

items.en: Fascinare meant to bewitch or put under a spell.
items.cn: fascinare 意为施魔法或使人中咒。

items.en: Fascinum was a spell or a charm against evil.
items.cn: fascinum 指咒语或辟邪的护符。

items.en: English fascinate meant to enchant by magic.
items.cn: 英语 fascinate 意为用魔法迷住。

items.en: The sense widened to mean charm or captivate.
items.cn: 词义扩大为使人倾心或着迷。

items.en: Fascinate now means to interest someone intensely.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fascinate 意为强烈地引起兴趣。

note.en: Fascinate is compared with related forms and with verbs for holding attention.
note.cn: 把 fascinate 与相关词形以及表示抓住注意力的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fascinate is the verb behind fascinating and fascination.
normalIntro.cn: fascinate 是 fascinating 与 fascination 背后的动词。

normal.en: Fascinate hides the sound of fascinating.
normal.cn: fascinate 与 fascinating 的发音相近。

normal.en: Be fascinated by means to be strongly attracted.
normal.cn: be fascinated by 意为被强烈吸引。

normal.en: A fascinating story holds the reader.
normal.cn: fascinating 的故事能抓住读者。

normal.en: Fascinate is stronger than interest.
normal.cn: fascinate 的语气比 interest 更强。

normal.en: Fascination is the feeling and the power to attract.
normal.cn: fascination 既指着迷的感觉，也指吸引力。

abstract.en: The force of fascinate lies in the idea of not being able to look away.
abstract.cn: fascinate 的力量来自「无法移开」这一动作。

abstract.en: From magic to charm, attention is held by something outside the self.
abstract.cn: 从魔法到魅力，注意力都被自身之外的东西掌控。

abstract.en: What fascinates us both attracts us and takes away our control.
abstract.cn: 让人着迷的事物既吸引人，也让人失去自主。

examples.en: Snakes fascinate many children.
examples.cn: 蛇让许多孩子着迷。

examples.en: She was fascinated by the old maps.
examples.cn: 她被那些旧地图深深吸引。

examples.en: The speaker fascinated the audience for an hour.
examples.cn: 演讲者让听众着迷了一个小时。

dict_mnemonic.text: fascinate 源自拉丁语 fascinare（施魔法），原义是「用魔法定住」，后来引申为「使人着迷」。

root: 源自拉丁语 fascinare（施魔法、蛊惑），核心义「用魔力定住目光与心神」。

sensesIntro.en: Fascinate means to attract someone strongly, to hold the gaze, or in older use to bewitch.
sensesIntro.cn: fascinate 意为强烈吸引某人、使目光无法移开，或在旧用法中施魔法蛊惑。

core.en: An attraction that holds attention and will not let go.
core.cn: 一种让人无法移开注意力的吸引力。

branches.en: Strong interest in something.
branches.cn: 对某物产生强烈兴趣。

branches.en: Attention fixed on a single sight.
branches.cn: 注意力固定在一个画面上。

branches.en: Magic that holds a person.
branches.cn: 用魔法控制一个人。

branches.en: Both describe attention one cannot break.
branches.cn: 两者都描述无法打断的注意力。

branches.en: Both suggest a force beyond ordinary will.
branches.cn: 两者都暗示超出意志的力量。

intro.en: Fascinate grows into nouns, adjectives, and adverbs about intense attraction.
intro.cn: fascinate 衍生出表示强烈吸引的名词、形容词与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fascinare, to bewitch, is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fascinare（施魔法）是直接词源。

items.example: We were fascinated by the film.
items.exampleCN: 我们被这部电影迷住了。
她讲了一个引人入胜的故事。
这本书细节丰富得令人着迷。

items.meaning: a state or power of strong attraction
items.example: His fascination with birds began young.
items.exampleCN: 他对鸟类的着迷始于幼年。

items.meaning: a decorative head covering, or a person who charms

items.example: His fascinations range from stars to shells.
items.exampleCN: 他着迷的东西从星星到贝壳都有。

definition_en: the popular style of clothes or behaviour at a time, a particular design, or a way of doing something
core_image: 时装秀的灯光下，模特走过长台，观众记录最新款式
scene: 她的裙子紧跟最新时尚。Her dress follows the latest fashion.
sceneCN: 这里 fashion 是「时尚」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她的裙子紧跟最新时尚。

senses.title: The prevailing style
senses.definition: the popular style of clothes, behaviour, or decoration at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期流行的服装、行为或装饰风格
senses.example: Short jackets are in fashion this year.
senses.exampleCN: 短夹克今年很流行。
senses.why: The central sense is a shared current style.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是当下被共同追随的风格。

senses.title: A style of clothing
senses.definition: a particular design or make of clothes
senses.definitionCN: 服装的某种设计或样式
senses.example: The dress is available in three fashions.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子有三种款式。
senses.why: The general style narrows to one garment design.
senses.whyCN: 总体风格缩小到某种服装设计。

senses.title: A way of doing something
senses.definition: a particular manner or method
senses.definitionCN: 某种特定的方式或方法
senses.example: He arranged the books in his own fashion.
senses.exampleCN: 他按自己的方式整理书籍。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a manner or way.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是方式或方法。

intro.en: Fashion comes from Latin facere, to make, through Old French façon, a making or manner.
intro.cn: fashion 源自拉丁语 facere（做），经古法语 façon（做法、样式）进入英语。

items.en: Facere meant to make or do.
items.cn: facere 意为做或制造。

items.en: Façon meant a making, a shape, or a manner.
items.cn: façon 意为制作、形状或方式。

items.en: Fashion meant a shape or a way of doing something.
items.cn: fashion 意为形状或做事的方式。

items.en: Fashion came to mean the current style of dress.
items.cn: fashion 开始指当下流行的服装风格。

items.en: Fashion covers clothing trends and any popular style.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fashion 涵盖服装潮流与各种流行风格。

note.en: Fashion is compared with similar-looking words and with words for style and trend.
note.cn: 把 fashion 与形近词以及表示风格和潮流的词作比较。

entries.definition: a small group within a larger one
a soft pad to sit or rest on
a distinctive way of doing or making

normalIntro.en: Fashion is the noun, fashionable is the adjective, and fashionably is the adverb.
normalIntro.cn: fashion 是名词，fashionable 是形容词，fashionably 是副词。

normal.en: In fashion means popular now.
normal.cn: in fashion 意为当下流行。

normal.en: A fashion show displays new clothes.
normal.cn: fashion show 展示新服装。

normal.en: Fashion and fashionable share the same base.
normal.cn: fashion 与 fashionable 同根。

normal.en: The ion ending often marks a noun.
normal.cn: ion 结尾常提示这是名词。

normal.en: Fashion can mean a way, not only clothes.
normal.cn: fashion 不只指衣服，也可指方式。

abstract.en: Fashion begins as a way of making, and becomes a way of looking.
abstract.cn: fashion 起初是制作方式，后来变成外观方式。

abstract.en: A style becomes fashion only when a group chooses it.
abstract.cn: 样式只有被群体选择后才成为时尚。

abstract.en: Trends change, but the act of following them does not.
abstract.cn: 潮流会变，但追随潮流这件事不会变。

examples.en: Short jackets are in fashion this year.
examples.cn: 短夹克今年很流行。

examples.en: She works in the fashion industry.
examples.cn: 她在时尚行业工作。

examples.en: He arranged the books in his own fashion.
examples.cn: 他按自己的方式整理书籍。

dict_mnemonic.text: fashion 源自拉丁语 facere（做），经法语 façon（做法、样式）而来，从「制作方式」演变为「时尚款式」。

root: 源自拉丁语 facere（做、制造），经古法语 façon（做法、样式），核心义「做出来的样子」。

sensesIntro.en: Fashion means the current popular style, a particular clothing design, or a manner of doing something.
sensesIntro.cn: fashion 意为当下流行风格、某种服装款式，或做事的方式。

core.en: A style that a group chooses and follows.
core.cn: 被一群人共同选择并追随的样式。

branches.en: The style most people follow.
branches.cn: 多数人追随的风格。

branches.en: A particular design of clothing.
branches.cn: 某种特定的服装设计。

branches.en: A personal manner of acting.
branches.cn: 个人做事的方式。

branches.en: Trends and garments reinforce each other.
branches.cn: 潮流与服装互相强化。

branches.en: Both are patterns people adopt.
branches.cn: 两者都是人们采纳的模式。

intro.en: Fashion has a family of adjectives, adverbs, and compounds.
intro.cn: fashion 拥有形容词、副词与复合词构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere, to make, is the distant root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere（做）是远源。

items.exampleCN: 这件外套现在显得过时。
这位时尚达人认识每位设计师。

items.example: The fashion show starts at eight.
The fashion designer won a prize.
items.exampleCN: 这位时装设计师获了奖。

definition_zh: 快的；迅速地；牢固的；禁食
definition_en: moving or happening quickly, firmly fixed, or to go without food for a period
core_image: 短跑运动员冲过终点线，计分牌亮出新的速度纪录
scene: 他跑得很快，赶上了第一班公交车。He ran fast and caught the first bus.
sceneCN: 这里 fast 是「迅速地」（第 2 个义项）；句意：他跑得很快，赶上了第一班公交车。

senses.title: Moving quickly
senses.definition: moving or able to move at high speed
senses.definitionCN: 移动或能够高速移动的
senses.example: She is a fast runner.
senses.exampleCN: 她跑得很快。
senses.why: The most familiar modern sense is high speed.
senses.whyCN: 最熟悉的现代义就是高速。

senses.title: At high speed
senses.definition: quickly, or at a high speed
senses.definitionCN: 快速地或高速地
senses.example: He ran fast to catch the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 他跑得很快去赶公交车。
senses.why: The adverb repeats the speed sense in action.
senses.whyCN: 副词义把速度义落实到动作上。

senses.title: Firmly fixed
senses.definition: firmly fixed or tightly closed
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢固定或紧紧关闭的
senses.example: The door was fast shut.
senses.exampleCN: 门紧紧地关着。
senses.why: The oldest sense is firmness, not speed.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是牢固，而非速度。

senses.title: To go without food
senses.definition: to eat no food, or little food, for a period
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内不吃或几乎不吃食物
senses.example: Some people fast for a day each month.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人每月禁食一天。
senses.why: A separate old verb meant to hold back from food.
senses.whyCN: 另一个古老动词义为节制饮食。

intro.en: Fast has two Old English sources: fæst, firm, and fæstan, to abstain from food.
intro.cn: fast 有两个古英语来源：fæst（牢固）与 fæstan（禁食）。

items.en: Fæst meant firm or fixed.
items.cn: fæst 意为牢固或固定。

items.en: Fæstan meant to abstain from food.
items.cn: fæstan 意为禁食。

items.en: The adverb fast meant firmly or close.
items.cn: 副词 fast 意为牢固地或靠近地。

items.en: Fast also came to mean quickly or eagerly.
items.cn: fast 也开始表示迅速地或急切地。

items.en: Fast now means quick, firm, or without food.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fast 意为快速、牢固或禁食。

note.en: Fast is compared with similar short words and with adjectives for speed.
note.cn: 把 fast 与形近短词以及表示速度的形容词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fast has three families: speed, firmness, and going without food.
normalIntro.cn: fast 有三组含义：速度、牢固与禁食。

normal.en: Fast food is served quickly.
normal.cn: 快餐上得很快。

normal.en: Hold fast means hold tightly.
normal.cn: hold fast 意为紧紧抓住。

normal.en: Fast asleep means deeply asleep.
normal.cn: fast asleep 意为熟睡。

normal.en: Breakfast breaks the night's fast.
normal.cn: 早餐打破一夜的禁食。

normal.en: Fasten is the verb built from fast.
normal.cn: fasten 是由 fast 构成的动词。

abstract.en: Speed and firmness meet in one short word.
abstract.cn: 速度与牢固在同一个短词里相遇。

abstract.en: To fast is to hold back from food, an older separate sense.
abstract.cn: 禁食义来自另一个更古老的义项，表示节制饮食。

abstract.en: The short form of fast makes it easy to use in compounds.
abstract.cn: fast 形式简短，便于构成复合词。

examples.en: The train is fast and comfortable.
examples.cn: 这趟列车又快又舒适。

examples.en: The rope held fast in the wind.
examples.cn: 绳子在风中牢牢固定。

examples.en: Farmers once fasted before the harvest.
examples.cn: 农夫们曾在收获前禁食。

dict_mnemonic.text: fast 的古义是「牢固」，hold fast 就是紧紧抓住；「快速」义后来从「有力地、急切地」发展出来；「禁食」来自另一个古英语动词。

root: 源自古英语 fæst（牢固的）与 fæstan（禁食），核心义分别涉及「牢固」与「节食」。

sensesIntro.en: Fast means quick, at high speed, firmly fixed, or to go without food.
sensesIntro.cn: fast 意为快的、迅速地、牢固地，或禁食。

core.en: A short word joining speed, firmness, and restraint.
core.cn: 一个把速度、牢固与节制连在一起的短词。

branches.en: A person or thing that moves quickly.
branches.cn: 移动很快的人或物。

branches.en: Acting at high speed.
branches.cn: 以高速行动。

branches.en: Held tightly in place.
branches.cn: 被牢牢固定在原位。

branches.en: Choosing not to eat for a time.
branches.cn: 在一段时间内选择不进食。

branches.en: The adjective and adverb share one idea of speed.
branches.cn: 形容词与副词共享同一个速度概念。

intro.en: Fast forms comparatives, a verb family, and common compounds.
intro.cn: fast 构成比较级、动词词族与常见复合词。

latinIntro.en: Old English fæst is the source; there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 fæst 是词源，fast 没有拉丁词根。

items.meaning: the act of going without food
items.exampleCN: 禁食是一种古老的习俗。

definition_zh: 脂肪；肥胖的；肥的；丰厚的
definition_en: a soft greasy substance in the body, having too much of it, or large and rich in amount
core_image: 厨房案板上一块厚厚的黄油，旁边是刚煎好的肉
scene: 这顿饭油脂太多，他吃得很饱。The meal had too much fat and left him full.
sceneCN: 这里 fat 是「脂肪」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这顿饭油脂太多，他吃得很饱。

senses.title: Grease in the body
senses.definition: a soft substance in the body used to store energy
senses.definitionCN: 身体中用于储存能量的柔软物质
senses.example: Too much fat raises health risks.
senses.exampleCN: 脂肪过多会增加健康风险。
senses.why: The core sense is the physical substance.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是具体的物质。

senses.title: Having too much body fat
senses.definition: weighing too much because of body fat
senses.definitionCN: 因体脂过多而体重超常的
senses.example: The fat goose waddled across the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 那只肥鹅摇摇摆摆地穿过院子。
senses.why: The adjective describes the body that holds the substance.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述承载这种脂肪的身体。

senses.title: Large or rich
senses.definition: large in amount, especially of money or profit
senses.definitionCN: 数量大，尤指金钱或利润丰厚
senses.example: The company made a fat profit.
senses.exampleCN: 公司赚了丰厚的利润。
senses.why: The idea of stored excess extends to money.
senses.whyCN: 储存过多的概念延伸到金钱。

intro.en: Fat comes from Old English fætt, meaning fattened or plump.
intro.cn: fat 源自古英语 fætt，意为养肥的或丰满的。

items.en: Fætt meant fattened or plump.
items.cn: fætt 意为养肥的或丰满的。

items.en: Fættian meant to make fat.
items.cn: fættian 意为使变肥。

items.en: Fat named the greasy substance in bodies and food.
items.cn: fat 指身体和食物中的油脂物质。

items.en: The adjective described animals and people.
items.cn: 形容词用于描述动物和人。

items.en: Fat also means large or rich in informal use.
items.cn: 现代非正式用法中 fat 还表示丰厚的、巨大的。

note.en: Fat is compared with similar short words and with words for being overweight or greasy.
note.cn: 把 fat 与形近短词以及表示肥胖或油脂的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fat is both the substance and the description that comes from it.
normalIntro.cn: fat 既是物质本身，也是由它产生的描述。

normal.en: Low-fat food has less fat.
normal.cn: 低脂食品含脂肪较少。

normal.en: Fat chance means very little chance.
normal.cn: fat chance 意为机会渺茫。

normal.en: Fatten means to make fat.
normal.cn: fatten 意为养肥。

normal.en: A fat salary is a large one.
normal.cn: fat salary 指丰厚的薪水。

normal.en: Fat sits at the front of fatty and fatten.
normal.cn: fat 位于 fatty 与 fatten 的词首。

abstract.en: Fat stores energy, so the word links body and supply.
abstract.cn: 脂肪储存能量，因此这个词连接身体与储备。

abstract.en: From body fat to rich profit, the idea is stored excess.
abstract.cn: 从体脂到丰厚利润，核心都是「储存的过剩」。

abstract.en: Fatness is a visible layer, which makes the word easy to extend.
abstract.cn: 肥胖是可见的层次，因此词义容易延伸。

examples.en: This cheese is high in fat.
examples.cn: 这种奶酪脂肪含量高。

examples.en: The cat grew fat on kitchen scraps.
examples.cn: 这只猫因吃厨房剩食而变胖了。

examples.en: He earned a fat salary as a manager.
examples.cn: 他当经理挣着丰厚的薪水。

dict_mnemonic.text: fat 是「脂肪」，fatten 是「养肥」，fatty 是「脂肪的」；低脂食品常说 low-fat。

root: 源自古英语 fætt（肥的、养肥的），核心义「身体或食物中的油脂」。

sensesIntro.en: Fat means the greasy substance in the body, a body that is overweight, or something large and rich.
sensesIntro.cn: fat 意为身体中的脂肪、肥胖的，或丰厚巨大的。

core.en: Stored grease that makes a body or food rich.
core.cn: 让身体或食物变得丰厚的储存油脂。

branches.en: The substance stored in the body.
branches.cn: 储存在身体中的物质。

branches.en: A body carrying much of that substance.
branches.cn: 携带大量这种物质的身体。

branches.en: A large amount of money or profit.
branches.cn: 大量金钱或利润。

branches.en: The substance and the body description are linked.
branches.cn: 物质与其身体描述相互联系。

branches.en: Excess and richness share one image.
branches.cn: 过剩与丰厚共享同一个意象。

intro.en: Fat forms adjectives and verbs about grease and weight.
intro.cn: fat 构成表示油脂与体重的形容词和动词。

latinIntro.en: Old English fætt is the source; there is no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 fætt 是词源，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: The fattest seal won the contest.
items.exampleCN: 最胖的海豹赢得了比赛。

items.example: Fatty food is hard to digest.

definition_en: a male parent, a male ancestor, a title for a priest, or the founder of something
core_image: 傍晚的院子里，父亲把孩子高高举过头顶，笑声惊起了树上的麻雀
scene: 傍晚的院子里，他把孩子举过头顶，笑声一直传到巷口。The father lifted his child high above his head.
sceneCN: 这里 father 是「父亲」（第 1 个义项）；句意：父亲把孩子高高举过头顶。

senses.title: A male parent
senses.definition: a man in relation to his child
senses.definitionCN: 与自己的孩子相对的男性家长
senses.example: His father taught him to swim.
senses.exampleCN: 他父亲教他游泳。
senses.why: The family sense is the oldest and most central use.
senses.whyCN: 家庭关系义是最古老、最核心的用法。

senses.title: A male ancestor
senses.definition: a man from whom a family or group is descended
senses.definitionCN: 家族或群体的男性先辈
senses.example: Their fathers came from the same village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的祖先来自同一个村庄。
senses.why: The parent sense stretches back along the family line.
senses.whyCN: 父亲义沿家族血脉向上延伸为祖先。

senses.title: A priest's title
senses.definition: a respectful title used for a priest
senses.definitionCN: 对神职人员的一种尊称
senses.example: Father John greeted the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 约翰神父迎接了来访者。
senses.why: Priests are addressed as fathers in the church tradition.
senses.whyCN: 教会传统中以父亲称呼神职人员。

senses.title: The founder of something
senses.definition: a person who starts or inspires a movement or field
senses.definitionCN: 开创或启发某项事业或领域的人
senses.example: He is called the father of the telephone.
senses.exampleCN: 他被称为电话之父。
senses.why: A founder stands at the beginning like a parent of the work.
senses.whyCN: 创始者像事业的家长一样站在起点上。

intro.en: Father goes back to Old English fæder and shares a very old root with many European languages.
intro.cn: father 可追溯到古英语 fæder，与许多欧洲语言共享一个非常古老的词根。

items.en: The root pəter named a father in the ancient ancestor language.
items.cn: 词根 pəter 在远古祖语中表示父亲。

items.en: The form fader carried the family sense into Germanic speech.
items.cn: fader 这一形式把家庭义带入日耳曼语。

items.en: Fæder was the everyday word for a male parent.
items.cn: fæder 是古英语中表示父亲的日常用词。

items.en: The spelling settled as fader and later father.
items.cn: 拼写先固定为 fader，后来变为 father。

items.en: Father also became a title for priests and a name for founders.
items.cn: 现代英语中 father 又成为神父的称呼和创始人的代称。

note.en: Father is compared with similar-looking words and with words for parents and ancestors.
note.cn: 把 father 与形近词以及表示父母、祖先的词作比较。

entries.definition: to a greater degree or distance
one of the light growths covering a bird
a person from whom one is descended

normalIntro.en: Father is the male parent, and the same word names priests and founders.
normalIntro.cn: father 是男性家长，同一个词也可指神父与创始人。

normal.en: Father and farther sound alike but mean different things.
normal.cn: father 与 farther 读音相近，但意思不同。

normal.en: Father Christmas is the British name for Santa Claus.
normal.cn: Father Christmas 是英式英语中对圣诞老人的称呼。

normal.en: A father figure is an older man who guides others.
normal.cn: father figure 指引导他人的年长男性。

normal.en: Fatherhood names the state of being a father.
normal.cn: fatherhood 指身为父亲的状态。

normal.en: Forefather adds fore to father to mean an ancestor.
normal.cn: forefather 在 father 前加 fore，表示祖先。

abstract.en: One word can name a parent, a priest, and a founder.
abstract.cn: 一个词可以同时指父亲、神父和创始人。

abstract.en: Kinship words often stretch toward honor and origin.
abstract.cn: 表示亲属的词常常延伸到敬意与起源。

abstract.en: Calling someone father is both a family tie and a sign of respect.
abstract.cn: 称某人为父亲既是家庭纽带，也是敬意。

examples.en: My father drives me to school every morning.
examples.cn: 我父亲每天早上开车送我上学。

examples.en: The visitors asked Father Thomas to lead the prayer.
examples.cn: 来访者请托马斯神父带领祈祷。

examples.en: She is regarded as the father of the project.
examples.cn: 她被视为这个项目的创始人。

dict_mnemonic.text: father 与德语 Vater 同源，都来自古代表示家庭男性长辈的词，核心是「一家之父」。

root: 源自原始印欧语 pəter（父亲），经日耳曼语与古英语 fæder，核心义「家庭中的男性长辈」。

sensesIntro.en: Father means a male parent, a male ancestor, a priest's title, or the founder of something.
sensesIntro.cn: father 意为父亲、男性祖先、神父的称呼，或某事物的创始人。

core.en: The male parent at the head of a family, and figures who take that role.
core.cn: 家庭中的男性家长，以及承担这一角色的形象。

branches.en: The man who raises a child.
branches.cn: 抚养孩子的男性。

branches.en: A male ancestor in the family line.
branches.cn: 家族血脉中的男性祖先。

branches.en: A respectful title for a priest.
branches.cn: 对神父的尊称。

branches.en: The person who begins or inspires something.
branches.cn: 开创或启发某事的人。

branches.en: Both the parent and the founder stand at the beginning of a line.
branches.cn: 父亲与创始人都站在某条脉络的起点。

intro.en: Father forms words for family roles, family states, and compound kinship terms.
intro.cn: father 构成表示家庭角色、身份状态与复合亲属称谓的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.example: Her father works in a hospital.
items.exampleCN: 她父亲在一家医院工作。

items.example: The fathers waited outside the classroom.

items.exampleCN: 他给了她慈父般的建议。

items.meaning: the state of being a father
items.exampleCN: 成为父亲改变了他的日常习惯。

items.example: The fatherless boy was raised by his aunt.
items.exampleCN: 这个没有父亲的男孩由姑妈抚养长大。
我祖父会讲古老的故事。

items.meaning: a man who marries one's mother
items.example: Her stepfather taught her to ride a bike.
items.exampleCN: 她的继父教她骑自行车。

items.example: The forefathers of the town built the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 这座小镇的祖先修建了那座桥。

items.example: He returned to his fatherland after years abroad.
items.exampleCN: 在国外多年后，他回到了祖国。

definition_en: a mistake, the blame for something wrong, a defect in a machine or system, or a break in rock layers
core_image: 工程师蹲在机器旁，手电筒照着烧焦的线路接头，眉头越皱越紧
scene: 机器突然停了，工程师顺着线路找到了烧坏的地方。A fault in the wiring stopped the machine.
sceneCN: 这里 fault 是「故障」（第 3 个义项）；句意：线路故障让机器停了下来。

senses.title: A mistake
senses.definition: something done wrongly or a flaw in what was done
senses.definitionCN: 做错的事或做好之事中的疏漏
senses.example: The report contained several faults.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告有几处错误。
senses.why: This is the broad everyday sense of something wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示「失误」的宽泛日常义。

senses.title: Blame or responsibility
senses.definition: responsibility for something bad that happened
senses.definitionCN: 对发生的坏事所负的责任
senses.example: The accident was not his fault.
senses.exampleCN: 这场事故不是他的过错。
senses.why: A fault is often the basis for assigning blame.
senses.whyCN: 过错常常是追究责任的依据。

senses.title: A defect or breakdown
senses.definition: a defect in a machine, system, or person
senses.definitionCN: 机器、系统或人身上的缺陷
senses.example: A fault cut the power to the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 一场故障让整条街都停了电。
senses.why: A mistake in a device becomes a technical fault.
senses.whyCN: 设备中的失误就成了技术故障。

senses.title: A break in rock
senses.definition: a crack in rock where the two sides have moved
senses.definitionCN: 岩层中两侧发生位移的裂缝
senses.example: The earthquake happened along a known fault.
senses.exampleCN: 地震发生在一条已知断层上。
senses.why: Geologists borrowed the word for a break in the earth.
senses.whyCN: 地质学家借这个词表示岩层的断裂。

intro.en: Fault came through Old French faute from Latin fallere, to deceive or fail.
intro.cn: fault 经古法语 faute 传入，源自拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、失误）。

items.en: Fallere meant to deceive, trick, or cause to fail.
items.cn: fallere 意为欺骗、蒙骗或使失败。

items.en: A popular noun form described a failure or defect.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语中用名词形式表示失误或缺陷。

items.en: Faute meant a lack, mistake, or offense.
items.cn: faute 意为缺失、错误或冒犯。

items.en: Fault entered English with the sense of a mistake.
items.cn: fault 以「错误」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word added senses of machine defects and rock breaks.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加了机械故障与岩层断层的义项。

note.en: Fault is compared with similar-looking words and with words for mistakes and defects.
note.cn: 把 fault 与形近词以及表示错误、缺陷的词作比较。

entries.definition: a curved roof or a secure room
a failure to do something required
an action or opinion that is wrong
a fault or weakness in something
a mistake, especially in writing or calculation

normalIntro.en: A fault is a mistake, the blame for it, a defect, or a break in rock.
normalIntro.cn: fault 指错误、应有的责任、缺陷，或岩层断层。

normal.en: Be at fault means to be responsible for a problem.
normal.cn: be at fault 意为对某个问题负有责任。

normal.en: To find fault with someone is to criticize them.
normal.cn: find fault with 某人意为挑剔对方。

normal.en: A fault line marks a crack in the earth.
normal.cn: fault line 标出地壳中的断裂带。

normal.en: Faulty adds -y to fault to mean full of faults.
normal.cn: faulty 由 fault 加 -y 构成，意为有缺陷的。

normal.en: A technical fault is a problem in a device.
normal.cn: technical fault 指设备中出现的问题。

abstract.en: A small mistake can grow into legal blame.
abstract.cn: 小失误可能演变为法律责任。

abstract.en: The same word covers a bad wire and a broken rock layer.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指坏掉的电线，也指断裂的岩层。

abstract.en: Naming a fault is often the first step to repair.
abstract.cn: 指出缺陷往往是修复的第一步。

examples.en: The engineers found a fault in the pump.
examples.cn: 工程师在泵里发现了一处故障。

examples.en: It was my fault that we were late.
examples.cn: 我们迟到是我的过错。

examples.en: The valley lies on a major fault.
examples.cn: 这条山谷位于一条主要断层上。

dict_mnemonic.text: fault 源自拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、失误），经古法语 faute 传入，词义从「失误」扩展到「责任」与「故障」。

root: 源自拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、失败），经古法语 faute，核心义「失误及其造成的缺陷与责任」。

sensesIntro.en: Fault means a mistake, blame for something, a defect in a machine, or a crack in rock.
sensesIntro.cn: fault 意为错误、应负的责任、机器缺陷，或岩层断层。

core.en: A failure or defect, together with the blame it brings.
core.cn: 失败或缺陷，以及由此产生的责任。

branches.en: Something done wrongly.
branches.cn: 做错的事情。

branches.en: Responsibility for what went wrong.
branches.cn: 对出错之事的责任。

branches.en: A defect that stops a device working.
branches.cn: 使设备无法运转的缺陷。

branches.en: A break where rock layers have moved.
branches.cn: 岩层发生移动的断裂。

branches.en: A mistake and the blame for it travel together.
branches.cn: 错误与由此而来的责任总是相伴。

intro.en: Fault forms words for defects, perfection, and the habit of finding blame.
intro.cn: fault 构成表示缺陷、完美以及挑剔习惯的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fallere and the popular noun fallita are the deeper sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 与通俗拉丁语名词 fallita 是更深的来源。

items.meaning: a mistake, defect, or to criticize

items.exampleCN: 检查员列出了三处缺陷。

items.example: The rock is faulted along the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 山脊沿线的岩层有断层。

items.meaning: the act of criticizing or forming faults
items.exampleCN: 不断挑剔损害了他们的友谊。
有故障的开关被换掉了。

items.example: Tests revealed the faultiness of the design.
items.exampleCN: 测试揭示了设计的缺陷。

items.meaning: the habit of looking for mistakes

definition_en: a kind act that helps someone, approval or support, or a preference shown to one side
core_image: 邻居隔着一道矮墙递来一篮刚摘的苹果，笑着说不用还
scene: 她帮邻居照看了一整天狗，邻居连声道谢。He asked me to do him a favour.
sceneCN: 这里 favour 是「恩惠；帮忙」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他请我帮他一个忙。

senses.title: A kind act
senses.definition: an act of kindness that helps another person
senses.definitionCN: 帮助他人的善意举动
senses.example: She did me a great favour last week.
senses.exampleCN: 她上周帮了我一个大忙。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of a helpful act.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示「帮忙」的日常核心义。

senses.title: Approval or support
senses.definition: approval of or support for a plan or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对计划或想法的赞同与支持
senses.example: Most voters are in favour of the change.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数选民赞成这项改变。
senses.why: To favour something is to look on it with approval.
senses.whyCN: favour 某事物就是对其抱赞同态度。

senses.title: Partiality
senses.definition: unfair support shown to one person or group
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某群体给予的不公平支持
senses.example: The coach showed favour to his old players.
senses.exampleCN: 教练偏袒他的老队员。
senses.why: Approval can slide into unfair preference.
senses.whyCN: 赞同可能滑向不公平的偏好。

senses.title: To prefer or support
senses.definition: to prefer one thing or to support a plan
senses.definitionCN: 偏爱某事物或支持某项计划
senses.example: The committee favours a later start.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会倾向于较晚开始。
senses.why: The noun sense becomes a verb of choosing sides.
senses.whyCN: 名词义转化为表示选择立场的动词。

intro.en: Favour comes from Latin favere, to be kind or show good will, through Old French.
intro.cn: favour 经古法语传入，源自拉丁语 favere（善待、表示好意）。

items.en: Favere meant to be well disposed toward someone.
items.cn: favere 意为对某人心怀善意。

items.en: Favur named kindness and good will.
items.cn: favur 表示善意与好意。

items.en: Favour entered English as a word for a kind act.
items.cn: favour 以「善举」之义进入英语。

items.en: The spelling favour settled in British English.
items.cn: 英式英语中固定了 favour 这一拼写。

items.en: The word also means approval and unfair partiality.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词还表示赞同与不公平的偏袒。

note.en: Favour is compared with similar-looking words and with words for kindness and approval.
note.cn: 把 favour 与形近词以及表示好意、赞同的词作比较。

entries.definition: the taste of a food or drink
a greater liking for one thing

normalIntro.en: A favour is a kind act, and to favour is to prefer or support.
normalIntro.cn: favour 是善意的帮助，作动词则表示偏爱或支持。

normal.en: Do me a favour is a polite request for help.
normal.cn: do me a favour 是请人帮忙的礼貌说法。

normal.en: In favour of means supporting an idea.
normal.cn: in favour of 意为支持某个想法。

normal.en: Curry favour means to seek someone's approval.
normal.cn: curry favour 意为讨好某人以求得认可。

normal.en: Favouritism is unfair preference for one person.
normal.cn: favouritism 指对某人的不公平偏袒。

normal.en: British spelling keeps the u in favour.
normal.cn: 英式拼写 favour 保留了字母 u。

abstract.en: A small act of help can become a lasting debt of gratitude.
abstract.cn: 一次小小的帮助可能变成长久的感激。

abstract.en: Approval and bias grow from the same root of good will.
abstract.cn: 赞同与偏见都源自同一种好意的根。

abstract.en: Favouring one side always means another side loses.
abstract.cn: 偏爱一方总意味着另一方有所失去。

examples.en: Could you do me a favour and close the window?
examples.cn: 你能帮我个忙，把窗户关上吗？

examples.en: Most members were in favour of the plan.
examples.cn: 大多数成员赞成这个计划。

examples.en: The judge must not show favour to either side.
examples.cn: 法官不得偏袒任何一方。

dict_mnemonic.text: favour 源自拉丁语 favere（善待、支持），经古法语 favur 进入英语，核心含义是「善意与支持」。
